lines.text: LOSS OF LIFE FOLLOWING MAN OVERBOARD FROM P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST
06May13
5. It is recommended that American Cruise Lines, Inc. update the Station Bill to assign one crew
member the responsibility of throwing the “Man Overboard" life buoy in event of a fall overboard. This
person should have other duties on or near the bridge. All crew should be trained to throw anything
buoyant immediately available to assist a person in the water.
6. It is recommended that American Cruise Lines, Inc. place a serviceable searchlight in the rescue boat.
7. It is recommended that American Cruise Lines, Inc. place a serviceable life ring in the port side main
deck life ring bracket.
8. It is recommended that American Cruise Lines, Inc. provide floating lights for all main deck life rings.
9. It is recommended that American Cruise Lines, Inc. develop an inclusive safety policy with regard to
authorized crew permitted to work on the stern in the vicinity of the paddlewheel. The policy should
designate in writing the “authorized persons" permitted in the area and detail specific evolutions requiring
access (ie. trash detail, mooring/sea detail, maintenance, etc.). A physical list of authorized persons
would deter others from accessing this dangerous area of the vessel, and provide an effective tool to
enforce the policy.
10. It is recommended that American Cruise Lines, Inc. provide physical barriers such as chains and
warning signs on both sides of the vessel as visual deterrents to prevent unauthorized access to the stern.
11. It is recommended that American Cruise Lines, Inc., in consultation with U.S. Coast Guard Marine
Safety Unit Portland Inspection Department, install effective deck lights (wired to the main deck lighting
controls) on the stern portion of the vessel. In the meaņtime, it is recommended that P/V QUEEN OF
THE WEST crew activate existing stern lights from sunset to sunrise every night.
12. It is recommended that American Cruise Lines, Inc., in consultation with U.S. Coast Guard Marine
Safety Unit Portland Inspection Department, consider developing a locking mechanism to prevent the
movement of the paddlewheel during swift current conditions. The mechanism should be developed only
if the risk of damage to the paddlewheel support arms or associated vessel propulsion machinery is
minimized.
13. It is recommended that the Master of P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST provide survival training and Man
Overboard training for all crew following a fall into the water.
14. It is recommended that the Master of P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST ensure all crew actively
participate in drills to ensure knowledge of man overboard recovery procedures.
15. It is recommended that the Master of P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST actively enforce the “authorized
personnel only" policy to prevent others from accessing the stern of the vessel. Enforcement should
include the use of effective and appropriate punishment and/or documentation of all personnel who
violate the policy.
16. It is recommended that the Master of P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST actively enforce all American
Cruise Lines, Inc. Operations Manual policies onboard P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST, but most notably
the following:
a. No drinking. Enforcement could include random alcohol tests when crew return from shore.
b. Crew in quarters after midnight. Enforcement could include watchmen keeping track of who is not
in quarters after midnight.
